title: refactor-ci-unify-lint-test-release-workflows-optimize-cache-and-bump-actions
author: Priya Desai
description: Consolidate and modernize our GitHub Actions workflows to reduce duplication, improve cache hit rates, and bump critical action versions for security and performance. Motivation: we've accumulated several slightly divergent CI workflows across packages that increase maintenance burden and make cache keys brittle. This PR: - Unifies lint, unit-test, and release orchestration into three well-scoped workflows (lint.yml, test.yml, release.yml) with sharable reusable job templates. - Bumps actions/checkout to v4 and actions/setup-node to v4 across the repo. - Stabilizes caching by standardizing cache key formats and adding per-package cache version metadata to control invalidation without changing workflow logic. - Reduces test matrix parallelism for heavy integration suites and introduces a default serial path for slow, flakey workloads. - Adds explicit retry logic for flaky network steps (npm install, docker pulls) and fallbacks for registry rate limits. - Removes deprecated custom OS matrix entries and consolidates node version testing to Node 18 and 20 (Node 16 removed per security EOL). Checklist: - [x] Consolidate workflows and add reusable templates - [x] Bump actions deps (checkout/setup-node/cache) - [x] Standardize cache keys and add version tag - [x] Reduce unnecessary matrix permutations - [x] Run full CI across monorepo and fix failures - [x] Add release automation gating to avoid accidental publishes Notes: This is primarily a repo hygiene and developer experience improvement. No production runtime code changed. Related work: ENG-4321 (CI reliability), ENG-4410 (release automation hardening).

release_notes: Consolidated CI workflows; bumped GitHub Actions to latest stable (checkout v4, setup-node v4); standardized cache keys to improve hit rates. No behavioral changes to runtime code. This should reduce CI maintenance and lower occasional cache-related failures.
